title: StuckJobsToProcessStuckJobs
description: One row of the DynamoDB jobs table as read back: each item the stuck-job Scan returns (check_stuck_jobs_to_db_jobs), read by check-stale-jobs. It describes the whole job record. Status moves received -> generating -> finishing -> completed, or to failed, by job-failed only, from any status but completed; the Scan returns only unfinished jobs. Transcript or summary text is never stored.

job_id.description: Huddle path: the Slack file ID. Manual path: lowercase hex SHA-256 (architecture §6).

channel_id.description: A Slack ID such as a channel, user or file ID.

thread_ts.description: Where to reply. Optional: the manual path may fall back to channel-level replies.

project_id.description: GitHub Project node ID, copied from the channel's link at claim time.

response_id.description: OpenAI background response ID (indexed by a GSI).

created_at.description: Unix seconds when the job was claimed.

ttl.description: Unix seconds after which DynamoDB deletes the record.

claimed_at.description: Unix seconds when the process-summary claim lease started. Absent or null once released. While the job is received, a later claim succeeds only after the lease has expired (90 seconds) or been released.

finishing_started_at.description: Unix seconds when the process-issues lease started. Absent or null once released. While the job is finishing, a later run takes over only after the lease has expired (180 seconds) or been released.

then.description: Once a background response exists, the job must know its project and response.

project_id.description: An external ID (GitHub node ID, OpenAI response ID): non-empty, no whitespace.

response_id.description: An external ID (GitHub node ID, OpenAI response ID): non-empty, no whitespace.
